To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we show clearly in the reconstiuted human system and the yeast system that the S305/P1073L mutations cause defects in mtDNA replisome activity and mtDNA replication, respectively.
the Alpers disease-associated S305R and the P1073 mutations in human Pol-γ cause defects in mtDNA synthesis by distinct mechanisms.

the Alpers syndrome mutations S305R and/or P1073L reduce DNA binding and/or catalytic efficiency of Pol-γ, and that P1073L reduces the mtDNA content in the heterozygous cells in both humanized yeast cells and in human cells, while S305R reduces the mtDNA replication efficiency in the humanized yeast cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms of mtDNA replication and repair, and the role of the mitochondrial DNA polymerase in human diseases.

the biochemical and physiological effects of the S305/P1073 compound mutation on the human mitochondrial DNA polymerases, and the implications of these results on the disease pathogenesis of Alpers syndrome.
understanding the molecular mechanisms by which the S305R and the P1073 L mutations in Pol-γ lead to the disease Alpers syndrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the S305 and P1073 mutations in POLG are associated with early childhood-onset disease by distinct mechanisms.
both the S305R and the P1073 mutations in the human POLG gene cause Alpers syndrome by different mechanisms.
the S305 mutation causes a defect in both the polymerase and the exonuclease activity, and the P1073 mutation causes a defect only in the polymerase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S305 and P1073 residues are important for the function of human DNA polymerase γ, and the P1073 mutation causes more severe phenotypic defects in mtDNA maintenance.
the S305 mutation in the human Pol-γ is the first example of the DNA binding defect in human DNA replication.
the S305 and P1073 mutations are associated with Alpers disease by different mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the S305/P1073 compound heterozygosity causes a more severe phenotype than either mutation by itself, and the severity depends upon the order of the mutations.
both the S305R and the P1073 mutations are deleterious, and their combined effects are more deleterious in the yeast system.
both the S305R and the P1073 mutant enzymes show defects in mtDNA maintenance and that the S305/P1073L mutant is more deleterious than the single mutant.
